project.name: CalebZone
project.title: CalebZone — implementation SRS
project.intro: A living software-requirements and implementation record for the CalebZone Java/Spring modular backend. The page joins the intended architecture with evidence from the current source tree, API contracts, gateway configuration and operational notes.
project.owner_note: Source documents are preserved in their original language. Configuration samples are sanitized before publishing.

modules.name: core
modules.role: Shared domain primitives, error model, validation, search specifications and reusable exception handling.

modules.name: auth
modules.role: Authentication, users, roles, permissions, JWT issuance and security-specific APIs.

modules.name: air
modules.role: Flight search bounded context with hexagonal ports, Redis cache, persistence and Sabre integration.

modules.name: ai-recognition
modules.role: Flight/search recognition service with reactive infrastructure and shared security/configuration patterns.

modules.name: gateway
modules.role: Reactive edge: routing, JWT verification, identity forwarding, rate limiting, retries, circuit breakers and observability.

requirements: Expose one client-facing gateway on port 8080 and route auth, air and AI traffic to independent services.
Allow explicitly public authentication and operational endpoints while requiring JWT authentication for all other exchanges.
Propagate a request id and verified identity context to downstream services without treating client-supplied identity headers as trusted.
Protect downstream capacity with Redis-backed rate limits, bounded retries and service-scoped circuit breakers.
Return a stable error contract with trace id, error category, localized message and field-level validation details.
Keep the flight search use case independent from Sabre, Redis and persistence through port-in/port-out boundaries.

architecture.diagram:
flowchart TB
  C[Client] --> G[Gateway :8080]
  G --> A[Auth :8081]
  G --> F[Air :8082]
  G --> AI[AI Recognition :8083]
  G -. rate limit .-> R[(Redis :6479)]
  F --> S[Sabre GDS]
  F --> D[(Flight data store)]
  A --> U[(User store)]
  G --> M[Prometheus / Actuator]
decisions: The gateway is the north-south policy and resilience boundary; each service still owns its domain behavior.
The air module follows a pragmatic hexagonal shape: web adapters call an input port, the application service orchestrates output ports, and adapters own external protocols.
Core owns the reusable error vocabulary and response construction; auth and air extend it for module-specific behavior and messages.
Redis is disposable control/cache state, not the source of truth for flight or user invariants.
The local project currently contains both documented intended behavior and implementation gaps; this SRS keeps those facts visible instead of silently treating every checklist item as shipped.
